BBugs found

Defects rather than taste, found on a live daemon; each is small and needs no decision.

B1 · Escape doesn't close menus, the Session commands sheet, or the session panel

The shared Sheet (views.rs:4214) has no key handler. The agent, model and mode menus, ⋮ and the panel stay open on Escape even with focus on their chip; only × or a click outside closes them. Quiet Ink's D15 says menus close on Escape.

B2 · The focus ring on composer chips is clipped into "( Auto )"

The chip row clips overflow, so the 2 px outline at 2 px offset shows only its left and right arcs. Use an inset ring (outline-offset: -2px) or give the row padding.

B3 · Phone New session: the help text slides under the Project row

At 390 px the paragraph's first line is hidden behind the Project select and the Runtimes | Skills switch.

B4 · Phone composer: the chips run under the send button

The model chip is cut off, and the mode and folder chips can't be reached. See P7 for the fix.

B5 · Settings shows a config warning as raw markdown in the accent colour

The backticks show literally, and indigo reads as a link. It should be an amber callout with rendered code (P6).

B6 · Tool headers show the command's backticks

Run `~/.local/bin/cookie-reinstall …`: the verb and its argument should be styled apart, with the argument in mono and no backticks (P3).

B7 · A session row's hover actions cover its title

On hover or right-click, ⋮, rename and delete sit on top of the title ("Persisten…") and the machine badge. Right-click should open D15's context menu at the pointer; hover should swap the time for a single ⋯ (P1).

B8 · The list orders by one time and shows another

Rows order by last_agent_activity (your last input) but show last_activity, so "1d ago" sits above "22h ago". Show the time the list orders by.

B9 · About 200 px of blank space around "earlier events not loaded"

The loader row sits in a tall empty block. Make it a single pill with normal spacing (P3).

B10 · The session panel's tabs wrap to two lines at 1440 px

Seven tabs in a 380 px panel leave "Events" alone on a second row. Fix in P4.

P1Sidebar: room for sessions

At 900 px tall the sidebar shows six sessions. Eight view links take about 300 px, and every row spends a second line on a machine badge and a path that are the same for all thirty sessions.

  • Views in two columns (Agents | Skills, Memory | Assets, …): four rows instead of eight. MCP servers becomes "MCP" to fit.
  • Search moves up beside New session, as an icon button; the Sessions heading keeps select, filter, and new folder. The filter shows as a chip, "7 days ▾", instead of the cut-off "Last 7 …".
  • One-line rows. The second line appears only when it adds something: a machine other than the project's usual one, or a folder other than the project's workspace. The time is short ("22h", "1d") and is the time the list orders by (B8).
  • State as a dot on the row's left: pulsing indigo while running, solid indigo when unread, amber while an approval waits. The spinner and the "completed" text go.
  • Hover swaps the time for ⋯, so actions never cover the title (B7); right-click opens the same menu at the pointer.
  • Read sessions are drawn in fg-2, unread ones in bold, so what's new stands out without a badge.

Questions (spec section 3; the user approved every answer on 2026-11-12)
  • Q1 The sidebar's views. Answer: two columns, four rows. Alternative: a collapsible "Workspace" group.
  • Q2 A row's second line. Answer: only when its machine or folder differs from the project's usual ones. Alternative: never; in the tooltip only.

P2New session: the composer first

Today, before you can type, the page shows a 60-word paragraph, four machine groups with runtime cards, eight tool chips (some indigo, some white, with no key to the colours), a tool budget line, and the skills list with switches. All of it matters, but almost always the defaults are right.

  • The composer sits in the middle of the page under a short heading, as every chat app does, with one line of chips for what the session will get: project, where it runs, folder, skills and tools. Each chip shows its current value.
  • "Runs on" opens the runtime picker, the same cards as today, grouped by machine, in a popover. Today's paragraph becomes one sentence at the popover's top.
  • Tools and skills fold into one "Tools & skills" popover. The tool chips get a legend: filled means offered up front, outlined means deferred (loaded through tool_search).
  • The Runtimes | Skills switch goes: the chips replace it.

P4Menus and the session panel

The chip menus are anchored to their chips, but they drop over the chip, list names in mono, and close only with ×. The ⋮ opens a full-height sheet for what is a short list of commands. The panel's seven tabs don't fit on one line.

  • Chip menus open above their chip, so the chip stays visible. Names in the sans, IDs only in the tooltip. The model menu gets a search field and, at its foot, the effort pill (P9, decided) instead of effort being part of each model's name. Try dragging it: the chip in the composer follows.
  • ⋮ opens a menu, not a sheet: actions first, then "Open in the session panel" with live values (18% · $4.78, 1 background call), then the agent's own commands. Type to filter, as today.
  • Panel tabs: icons, with a label only on the active tab, and counts as small badges, so seven fit on one line at 380 px (B10). The Usage tab leads with three summary tiles before the full table.
  • Escape, a click outside, and Back close any of them (B1).

Questions (spec section 3; the user approved every answer on 2026-11-12)
  • Q5 The header's ⋮. Answer: a menu anchored to ⋮. Alternative: the Session commands sheet, restyled.

P5Workspace views: one pattern for all of them

Each view lays itself out differently. Agents is a two-pane list with the primary button top-left; MCP puts a full-width button under its list; Machines and Schedules put it top-right; Memory is a centred list with a trash icon on every row; Sharing is centred text. Widths range from 480 to 1200 px, and two titles don't match their sidebar entries ("Machines & runtimes", "Scheduled prompts").

  • One view header: the title as in the sidebar, one sentence on what the view is for, and actions top-right with the primary one last. One content width (880 px).
  • One list row: an icon, the name in the sans, tags, one line of description, quiet meta on the right, and ⋯ on hover (and right-click). Agents' three bordered buttons per row and Memory's always-visible trash go into ⋯.
  • Search and a segmented filter under the header wherever a list can grow (Agents, Memory, Skills, Assets).
  • Agents: grouped into Yours / Official / ACP, each row saying what the agent does and which model it uses. The editor opens full width with a Form | File switch: a form for description, mode, models and permissions, and the raw file for anything else.
  • Machines: no cards inside cards. A machine is a heading; its runtimes are rows.
  • Schedules: the schedule in words, the cron line as quiet mono, an on/off switch per row, and recent runs below.

P6Settings

Settings has three columns: the app's sidebar, Settings' own list, then the content. Model rows put a mono ID and a Change button in a stack that doesn't line up, and a config warning shows as raw markdown in indigo (B5).

  • Settings takes over the sidebar while open ("← Back to sessions" at the top, as in Linear or Slack), so the content gets the width. The connection and version sit at the foot.
  • Each row is label + description on the left, one control on the right. A model is a single picker showing the model's display name and effort, with a reset icon when it differs from the default. The config.key stays, faint, under the description.
  • Fields show their real value; a placeholder says "not set" or "30m · default" in the faint colour, so it can't be mistaken for a value.
  • Warnings are amber callouts with rendered code and a fix-it action where there is one.

P7Phone

The phone layout works, but the composer's chips don't fit (B4), the drawer's eight view tiles leave room for one or two sessions, and New session puts the composer under a long scroll of cards with clipped help text (B3).

  • One composer chip on a phone, "claude · Opus 5.5 · Auto", opening one bottom sheet with agent, model, effort, mode and folder. Nothing hides behind the send button.
  • Drawer: New session as a full-width button; the views as one horizontally scrolling row of pills instead of a 4×2 grid; sessions get the rest, at a finger-sized 44 px per row.
  • New session: the composer at the bottom where the thumb is, with the "where" chips (P2) in a scrolling row above it.
  • Header badges are icon + number only; the sidebar button carries the unread dot.

Questions (spec section 3; the user approved every answer on 2026-11-12)

P8Type and details

Quiet Ink's D11 moved labels to the sans, but monospace is still everywhere a name appears: agent names in Agents, the mode menu's options, runtime cards ("global/global"), Memory's names, the New session footer ("global only: no workspace"), and the model IDs in Settings.

  • Mono only for what you would type: code, commands, paths, config keys, IDs. Names (agents, memories, runtimes, modes, models) use the sans.
  • Display names over IDs: "Claude Opus 5.5 · High" rather than anthropic/claude-opus-5-5 (high); the ID goes in the tooltip and the editor.
  • Tags with one meaning per colour: indigo means a kind (primary), green a healthy state (ready, connected), amber something to look at (customized, waiting), grey anything else. Today indigo also marks tools offered up front and inactive tabs.
  • Times: short and relative in lists ("22h"), absolute in tooltips; the same time the list orders by (B8).
  • Hover-only actions get a right-click twin everywhere (D15 already covers most), and every ⋯ reaches the same items.

P9The effort control: a sliding pill decided D1, D2

One control chooses a native model's variant and an ACP agent's effort alike: a draggable segmented pill at the foot of the model menu. The composer chip shows the model and the variant's name, nothing else. Drag the pill, click a segment, or use the arrow keys; the colour warms from indigo toward orange as effort rises.
